content_voiceover: This table is the classic boards framework for the four mechanisms of drug-induced hemolysis or a positive DAT, and you should be able to name the prototype drug for each. Drug adsorption, or hapten mechanism, prototype drug is penicillin, especially at high doses, the drug binds covalently to the red cell membrane as a cell-bound hapten, and the antibody only reacts with drug-coated cells. DAT is typically IgG-positive, and the clinical course is subacute onset with mild to severe hemolysis. Neoantigen, or immune complex, or ternary complex mechanism, prototype drug is quinidine or stibophen, here the antibody binds the drug-RBC complex together, reacting only when drug is present, DAT is typically complement-only, and the presentation is acute onset with severe hemolysis, this is the mechanism behind sudden brisk intravascular hemolysis with a new drug exposure. Autoimmune mechanism, prototype drug is alpha-methyldopa, the drug induces a truly drug-independent RBC autoantibody, so the antibody is a panagglutinin that reacts even without the drug present, DAT is IgG, and onset is insidious with chronic, mild hemolysis, this is the one that behaves just like idiopathic warm AIHA, which is why methyldopa was highlighted on the previous slide. Finally nonimmune protein adsorption, prototype first-generation cephalosporins, the drug modifies the RBC membrane causing nonspecific protein adsorption, DAT is non-immunoglobulin, and there is no true hemolysis, this is a serologic red herring, a positive DAT without clinical hemolysis.
keypoints: Drug adsorption/hapten (penicillin): drug is cell-bound hapten, Ab reacts only with drug-coated RBCs, IgG DAT
Neoantigen/ternary complex (quinidine): Ab binds drug+RBC together, complement DAT, acute severe hemolysis
Autoimmune (methyldopa): drug induces drug-independent panagglutinin, IgG DAT, insidious chronic hemolysis
Nonimmune adsorption (1st-gen cephalosporins): nonspecific protein adsorption, non-Ig DAT, no hemolysis
keypoint_voiceover: Four mechanisms, four prototype drugs. Drug adsorption or hapten mechanism is penicillin, the antibody only reacts when drug is stuck to the cell, giving an IgG-positive DAT with subacute hemolysis. Neoantigen or ternary complex mechanism is quinidine, antibody binds drug and red cell together, complement-only DAT, and acute severe intravascular hemolysis. Autoimmune mechanism is methyldopa, the drug triggers a truly drug-independent panagglutinin, IgG DAT, insidious chronic hemolysis identical to warm AIHA. And nonimmune adsorption is first-generation cephalosporins, nonspecific protein sticks to the membrane, DAT is non-immunoglobulin, and importantly there is no actual hemolysis, just a confusing positive DAT.
